p07-orphan-descendant.ambiguity: §5.5 'the orphan's descendants are NOT auto-orphaned'. Does the descendant's OWN effects then apply, or is it excluded because its ancestor is missing?
p07-orphan-descendant.declared_split: kid-applies -> y present ; whole-branch-excluded -> y absent

p10-id-whitespace-and-separators.ambiguity: §1 says ids must be free of \n and :. Is that enforced (reject) or merely documented? The corpus cannot tell, but a port that rejects and a port that accepts will diverge on a hostile input.

p17-cycle-descendant.ambiguity: 5.5: 'cycle-affected records are orphans'. Does that include a record DOWNSTREAM of a cycle, or only the members? (Clause 2 of the two-clause rule: Kahn non-emission is transitive.)
p17-cycle-descendant.declared_split: cycle members only -> orphans=[ca,cb], y enters state ; transitive -> orphans=[ca,cb,down]

p18-descendant-of-orphan-vs-descendant-o.ambiguity: The PAIR that proves two clauses are needed. A descendant of a MISSING parent must apply; a descendant of a CYCLE must not. They differ only in whether the parent exists.
p18-descendant-of-orphan-vs-descendant-o.declared_split: both apply -> y AND z in state ; only the cycle branch excluded -> orphans=[ca,cb,dn], state={y:2}

p19-self-loop-descendant.ambiguity: A self-parented record: is it a cycle member, and is its child a cycle descendant?
p19-self-loop-descendant.declared_split: a orphan only -> k applies ; transitive -> orphans=[a,k]
